> The spec nor the error imply this, where did you find this out? All it says is that it needs to be an `xdg_toplevel`, not that it has to be mapped.

This is merely a speculation based on the error message and the following explanation.

> [Only xdg_toplevel equivalent surfaces may be exported, otherwise an invalid_surface protocol error is sent.](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-foreign-unstable-v2#zxdg_exporter_v2:request:export_toplevel) 

> [The identifier is only valid as long as the toplevel is mapped. If the toplevel is unmapped the identifier must not be reused. ](https://wayland.app/protocols/ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1#ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1:event:identifier) (Although ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 is not yet supported by my compositor, I still think it is of reference value.)


```
zxdg_exporter_v2@17: error 0: surface must be an xdg_toplevel
```

Note that the error code for [`invalid_surface`](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-foreign-unstable-v2#zxdg_exporter_v2:enum:error:entry:invalid_surface) is `0`.

> On what compositor can you replicate this issue? Maybe it's some compositor-specific quirk.

Cinnamon (muffin 6.6.7  [cinnamon-6.6.7-wayland-info.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26290710/cinnamon-6.6.7-wayland-info.txt) ) and sway (1.9 [sway-1.9-wayland-info.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26290711/sway-1.9-wayland-info.txt))


> Additionally, does it happen if the exporter is created after committing the surface but before configuration?

Yes, it is still crashing. The error messages and backtrace are similar.

Note: AI assistance was used in investigating this issue.

> This is merely a speculation based on the error message and the following explanation.

Oh that's fine no worries. That said I think that the issue is somewhere else.

> [The identifier is only valid as long as the toplevel is mapped. If the toplevel is unmapped the identifier must not be reused. ](https://wayland.app/protocols/ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1#ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1:event:identifier)(Although ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 is not yet supported by my compositor, I still think it is of reference value.)

This protocol is used for different things and follows different rules. I haven't double-checked, but if not otherwise specified, I think that it's perfectly reasonable to assume that the handles from both protocols are unrelated and technically incompatible.

> Note: AI assistance was used in investigating this issue.

Next time, please make this and the fact that it's speculation clearer.

---

I can see that you have added some `LIBDECOR_ENABLED` guards. I assume that it didn't build before (it's rarely checked) and I guess that you're running without it? I can't replicate it either on sway 1.11 with and without `GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_LIBDECOR=1`.

Could you please send me the result of `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 path/to/godot --verbose 2>&1 debug.log`? Please note that it's a protocol dump and includes all input sent to the engine.

> I can see that you have added some `LIBDECOR_ENABLED` guards. I assume that it didn't build before (it's rarely checked) and I guess that you're running without it? I can't replicate it either on sway 1.11 with and without `GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_LIBDECOR=1`.
